cases.purpose: Repeat version, option and dry-run parity under a proven FITRIM-killing filter; assert candidate child resolves fstrim to the builtin and exercise additional size boundaries.
cases.oracle: util-linux 2.41 fstrim(8) on the reference side (same guest, same per-side tmpfs mounts, same fixture tables); the kernel decides mountpoint, permission and FITRIM results identically for both sides.
cases.comparison: Byte parity of status, stdout and stderr: each invocation is bracketed by "[label]" markers on both streams and followed by its exit status; no normalisation. The whole matrix runs in one shell under a seccomp filter that kills it with SIGSYS on FITRIM (the remaining markers would be missing and the shell status would be 159), so the dry runs and usage errors are shown to make no FITRIM request on either side; setup proves the kill rule. --version output is compared too: a different version string is a real difference. Candidate child verifies builtin resolution and fails control if it is absent.

files.fitrim_probe.py:
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# Setup control (pane 214): FITRIM on PATH under the caller's seccomp rules
# must give WANT (ok or an errno name). Usage: fitrim_probe.py PATH WANT
import errno, fcntl, os, struct, sys
fd = os.open(sys.argv[1], os.O_RDONLY | os.O_CLOEXEC)
try:
    fcntl.ioctl(fd, 0xc0185879, bytearray(struct.pack('QQQ', 0, 2 ** 64 - 1, 0)))
    code = 0
except OSError as error:
    code = error.errno
os.close(fd)
want = 0 if sys.argv[2] == 'ok' else getattr(errno, sys.argv[2])
if code != want:
    print('CONTROL-FAILED FITRIM errno %d, wanted %s' % (code, sys.argv[2]))
    sys.exit(98)
print('mechanism control ok')
files.opts.sh:
if [[ ${FSTRIM_EXPECT_BUILTIN:-0} == 1 ]]; then
  [[ $(type -t fstrim) == builtin ]] || { echo "CONTROL-FAILED candidate fstrim is not builtin"; exit 98; }
fi
r() { local label=$1; shift; echo "[$label]"; echo "[$label]" >&2; "$@"; echo "[$label] status=$?"; }
r sizes fstrim -n -o 0x1000 -l 1MiB -m 4KB /tmp

cases.script:
export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
H=/opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/system-seccomp.py
r() { local label=$1; shift; echo "[$label]"; echo "[$label]" >&2; "$@"; echo "[$label] status=$?"; }
/usr/bin/python3 "$H" --kill ioctl:1=0xc0185879 -- "$BASH" --noprofile --norc opts.sh
s=$?; echo "shell status=$s"
[[ $s == 0 ]] || exit "$s"
